title: Tenant memory scenario simulator: dynamic headroom, KV compaction & activation budgeting
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: build a reproducible scenario-driven memory simulator that models per-tenant GPU memory split across model weights, KV cache, and transient activations under continuous batching. Output should be prescriptive: per-tenant headroom targets, KV compaction thresholds, and batch size recommendations to meet latency SLOs while minimizing token cost. Acceptance criteria: 1) Simulator can ingest p99/p50 request size and concurrency traces and produce a memory pressure curve; 2) Generates per-tenant policy suggestions (KV retention time, compaction aggressiveness, activation reservation) and an expected cost/latency delta; 3) Validation against a controlled cluster experiment shows simulator predictions within ±10% for peak memory and ±15% for p99 latency; 4) Exportable report and a lightweight API consumed by autoscaler and admission controller.
approach: 1) Ingest anonymized production traces (sequence length distribution, inter-arrival times, tenant id, model type). 2) Model weights as fixed baseline per model variant, KV occupancy as function of active sessions * target retention + prefix reuse multiplier, activations as transient memory proportional to batch composition and max_decode_length. 3) Implement event-driven simulator that steps through request timeline applying continuous batching rules (max batch size, batching delay), KV insert/evict rules, and backpressure when headroom breached. 4) Run Monte Carlo on 500 synthetic tenant traces to derive robust headroom percentiles. 5) Translate outputs to policy suggestions (e.g., KV-retain-ms, compaction-threshold-percent, min-activation-reserve-MiB) and a confidence score.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - We decided to model KV eviction as time + size hybrid rather than pure LRU to capture tenant-level fairness. This simplifies simulator state and closely matches observed production behaviour for multi-tenant workloads. - Chose event-driven discrete simulation (memory/time steps) over full GPU kernel emulation to keep runtime tractable for thousands of scenarios. - Will not model exact kernel-level memory fragmentation initially; instead we add a headroom fudge factor derived from historical fragmentation measurements. - Default confidence band set to 90%: recommendations will include a conservative headroom buffer; we will later expose an aggressive mode for non-critical tenants.
metrics_and_success: Primary metrics: predicted_peak_memory_error_pct (target <=10%), predicted_p99_latency_error_pct (target <=15%), mean_token_cost_delta_estimate (expected -8% to -12% for top 20 tenants), false_positive_headroom_increase_rate (target <5%). Operational success: simulator integrated into 2-week canary of autoscaler and used to reduce reserved capacity for low-impact tenants.
comments: 2025-02-15 — Aisha Malik: Scoped ticket, added acceptance criteria and initial approach. Requested anonymized trace export from infra. Assigned Tomás to prototype the event-driven simulator.

2025-02-20 — Tomás Rivera: Prototype complete for single-tenant trace. Early results show KV dominance for long prefix reuse tenants (KV >= 45% of total footprint). Pushed draft PR to runtime-sim with basic batching rules implemented.

2025-02-25 — Li Chen (SRE): Uploaded anonymized 30-day trace bucket and provided a step function of fragmentation headroom observed per GPU instance. Suggested adding a per-model weight-slice ledger to account for quantized vs full weights.

2025-03-03 — Product review (Maya Ortiz): Reviewed initial simulator outputs. Requested customer-facing policy templates (Safe/Default/Aggressive) and a UI export for Console to preview suggested KV policies.

2025-03-08 — Tomás Rivera: Ran Monte Carlo across 300 synthetic tenant traces. Median predicted_peak_memory_error_pct = 8.6%, predicted_p99_latency_error_pct = 12.1%. Found worst-case mismatch with heavy short-sequence burst patterns; added micro-burst smoothing to batching model.

2025-03-11 — Security (Rahul Patel): Quick review — no PII in traces. Recommended documenting retention and scrub steps in design doc. Marked ticket security_review_required=false for now but flagged for audit if integrated into private deploy flow.

2025-03-12 — Aisha Malik: Decision log: proceed to build a lightweight API endpoint for autoscaler integration and a CSV export for Console. Plan canary with 10 non-critical tenants next quarter. Added release target runtime-1.22.

2025-03-12 — Tomás Rivera: Next actions: finalize PR, add unit tests for KV compaction policy generator, create dataset of 100 anonymized tenant traces for canary, schedule cluster experiment with infra for 2025-03-25 run.
